title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not Grothendieck's own mathematics. It is page 96 of a typed English translation of a Russian paper, inserted into a folder whose neighbouring pages are Grothendieck's manuscript notes on the Galois theory of motives over F_q (Frobenius eigenvalues, weights, the groups M(q)). The marginal 'p. 218' is very likely the page number of the original Russian publication. The title and content point to B. G. Moishezon's paper on a criterion of projectivity for complete abstract algebraic varieties (Izv. Akad. Nauk SSSR, 1964; English translation in AMS Translations). I infer this from the content rather than from a reference printed on the page.

Step 1. The page restates the Nakai–Moishezon ampleness criterion as a consequence of 'theorem 2'. Let V be a smooth complete variety of dimension s and D a divisor on V. Suppose D^k·W > 0 for every irreducible subvariety W of dimension k, for k = 1,...,s (for k = s this means D^s > 0). Then for n large, the linear system |nD| gives a closed embedding of V into projective space. In other words, D is ample and V is projective.

Step 2. Chapter III then begins an application. Take V complete and normal of dimension s, and U ⊂ V a dense open subset that is quasi-projective, embedded via homogeneous coordinates x_0, x_1, ... with x_0 ≠ 0 on the chart. Set F_j = x_j/x_0 and let {F} be the k-linear span of the F_j. Let T_l be the irreducible divisorial (codimension-one) components of the boundary V − U. Define τ_l = min_j ord_{T_l}(F_j), the minimal pole/zero order of the coordinate functions along T_l.

Step 3. The page breaks off just as a function φ ∈ {F} with prescribed orders along the T_l is being chosen. Presumably the aim is to build, from the hyperplane class on U and boundary multiplicities like Σ τ_l T_l, a divisor on V to which the numerical criterion can be applied. This would give conditions for a compactification of a quasi-projective variety to be projective.

The handwritten interventions are minor: 'a' corrected to 'the' before 'linear space', an 'l' in the margin, and the formula τ_l = min_j n_{T_l}(F_j) written in by hand. They look like a reader's or translator's corrections, not mathematical additions.
errors: No mathematical errors visible. Notational inconsistencies only: the handwritten formula uses n_{T_l} while the typed text uses n_{T_1}, T_1; and 'k = 1,s' with an overbar is Russian notation for k = 1,...,s.
Archival note: the page is misfiled or intercalated among Grothendieck's motive notes. Its content is unrelated to the neighbouring pages on Frobenius weights and the motivic Galois group over F_q.

ideas.what: Numerical criterion for ampleness: D^k·W > 0 for all irreducible subvarieties W of dimension k implies nD is very ample for large n
ideas.where_published: Not Grothendieck's; Moishezon, Izv. Akad. Nauk SSSR 1964 (English transl. AMS Translations); Nakai, Amer. J. Math. 1963

ideas.what: Studying projectivity of a normal compactification V of a quasi-projective U via the orders of the coordinate functions along the boundary divisors T_l
ideas.modern_name: Boundary-divisor construction for projectivity of compactifications

deep.surprise_reason: This is a typed translation of someone else's published paper (apparently Moishezon's projectivity criterion), with only trivial handwritten edits. It contains no Grothendieck mathematics. The only curiosity is archival: it sits inside the 1965 motives folder.
transcription_corrections: Typed text has n_{T_1}(F_j) and 'divisor T_1' (subscript 1), while the handwritten formula uses T_l. The intended index is l throughout; the margin 'l' appears to be a correction to this effect.
'{T_l}' in the typed text is hand-corrected to l.
'p. 218' in the left margin is a reference to the original publication's pagination, not to this archive.
